newsitem.title: FRANCE: France shifts development aims away from Paris.
newsitem.headline: France shifts development aims away from Paris.

text.p: The French government, turning its back on opera houses and other grand Paris-centred schemes, unveiled long-term plans on Thursday to improve the country's roads and ports and install computers in schools.

Conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe, presiding at a meeting of ministers to define regional development projects to the year 2015, said France should "should adapt by taking account of two factors... decentralisation and European construction".
"Regional development policy should be more supple and less interventionist," Juppe said, adding that ending the isolation of French regions "does not mean launching pharaonic projects".

He took a swipe at the grand projects of late president Francois Mitterrand, including the Bastille opera house, a giant library by the Seine, a glass pyramid entrance to the Louvre Museum and sprawling science and music cities in Paris.

He said that the "almost exclusively Parisian sites" were "no doubt useful but also no doubt excessive." Juppe took office in 1995 after President Jacques Chirac succeeded Socialist Mitterrand, who had ruled since 1981.

Juppe's plans call for computers to be installed in all schools by the year 2000, adding details to a goal set by President Jacques Chirac. Each primary school should have a computer per 30 children, each high school one per 10 students.
The ministers met in the southwestern town of Auch, 600 km (400 miles) from Paris in the most rural part of France.
Their draft scheme also sets goals like better links between French regions and other European centres, currently linked most strongly to Paris by air, road and rail.

But he cautioned that ending regional isolation "does not mean that each department must be crossed by motorways, furrowed by high speed trains and a huge canal with an international airport as the icing on the cake".
Among the other targets agreed in outline were:
-- Transferring 30,000 public sector jobs out of the Paris area by the year 2000.
-- Creating a bank for developing small and medium-sized businesses. The bank would have a fund of one billion francs ($200 million) over two years.
-- Promoting regions that will host the soccer World Cup in June and July 1998. A credit of 10 million francs ($2.0 million) would be available for this year.
-- Developing roads along the Atlantic coast. Improving port services.
-- Improving regional airports for international flights, bolstering Paris airports as European hubs.
-- Aid for major cities to help to draw and keep headquarters of major companies in France.
-- Stepping up environmental protection, by protecting farm and forest land, improving water quality, increasing electrification of transport.
